name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund spread 153.9bp on 6 Nov, above the 150bp Alert line but below its 174.6bp peak of 22 Oct
state: France's 10-year yield was 4.76% on 6 Nov against 3.22% on the Bund, a spread of 153.9bp, above the 150bp Alert line. It was 148.2bp on 5 Nov and peaked at 174.6bp on 22 Oct (Banque de France and Bundesbank data via Ideal Investisseur). Fitch moved France's A+ outlook to negative on 30 Oct (Sovereign Magazine), citing deteriorating public finances and political uncertainty (Trading Economics). No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying was found as of 8 Nov.
for_you: Higher French borrowing costs feed into budget choices and French bank funding. Holders of euro-area government bonds, and funds that own them, are exposed to further swings in spreads.

sources.title: Ideal Investisseur — OAT / Bund spread today

Sovereign Magazine — France credit rating: Fitch negative outlook

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
